The standardised advantage is defined in **Definition 4.2 (GRPO Gradient)** on **page 5**.

**Setup:** For an input x from task i, the model generates G group-wise rollouts {y_k}, k = 1…G. Let r_{i,k}(x) be the reward for the k-th sample (p. 5).

**Group mean:**

  μ_{r_i}(x) = (1/G) Σ_{k=1}^{G} r_{i,k}(x)

**Group standard deviation:**

  σ_{r_i}(x) = √[ (1/G) Σ_{k=1}^{G} ( r_{i,k}(x) − μ_{r_i}(x) )² ]

The normalisation inside the square root is **1/G**, so this is the population standard deviation, not the 1/(G−1) sample version (p. 5).

**Standardised advantage:**

  Â_{i,k}(x) = ( r_{i,k}(x) − μ_{r_i}(x) ) / σ_{r_i}(x)

(p. 5)

**Properties the paper derives from this definition:**
- **Zero-sum:** Σ_{k=1}^{G} Â_{i,k}(x) = 0 (Eq. 4, p. 5).
- **Unit mean square:** (1/G) Σ_{k=1}^{G} Â²_{i,k} = 1, so Σ_{k=1}^{G} Â²_{i,k} = G (p. 16). This follows because σ uses the 1/G normalisation. The proof of the RL interference upper bound relies on it (pp. 16–17).

In the experiments, G = 16 rollouts per prompt (p. 13).
